description: Painted sprite parts for the patrol king (?art=paint). Same three steps as paint-rebel-pawn.json, plus the crown as its own part so the checkmate finale can throw it off; then tools/art/cut-parts.mjs.

steps.name: pose
steps.prompt: Full-body game sprite of the royal patrol KING from the first image, painted in the art style of the second image (a character select sheet). Use the third image only for the full-body pose and chunky proportions, not for its style. SUBJECT: the stern king of the royal patrol. A tall jewelled gold crown with ball-tipped points and coloured gems on its band. Under it a sculpted steel-grey face mask covering the whole face, with two narrow squinting eye slits, a painted brown handlebar moustache and a small pointed goatee; thick brown curls frame the mask on both sides. A gold cape fastened at the collar by two round gold clasps, draped over both shoulders and hanging behind him to his calves so it shows past his back and on both sides of the robe, over a long royal-blue robe with a gold centre stripe and gold hem, short dark boots. A steel sword with a narrow straight blade and a curled gold crossguard, held upright in his right fist on the right side of the figure: the bare skin fist clearly wraps around the grip just under the crossguard, the blade rises straight up above the fist and a round gold pommel shows below the fist. Standing, three-quarter view facing right, feet visible, chunky and big-headed: the head and crown are about half the figure's height. STYLE to match the second image exactly: bold flash-era 2D brawler cartoon, very thick even black outlines, flat fills, one hard cel shadow, crisp white highlights on metal, polished royal blue with gold trim, no damage. One character only, centred, on a plain flat light grey background (#d8d8d8), no ground, no cast shadow, no text, no labels, no frame.

steps.name: parts
steps.prompt:
Cut this exact character into separate parts for a 2D cut-out puppet, like a paper-doll sprite sheet. Keep his exact art style, colours, outline thickness and shading. Draw each part whole and complete, including the bits that are normally hidden behind other parts, and give every part its own very thick black outline all the way round. The parts are separate stickers with wide empty gaps between them, every part at the same scale as in the first image, on a plain flat light grey background (#d8d8d8). The image holds only these parts and nothing else: no other characters, no tiles, no text, no labels, no numbers, no grid lines, no cast shadows.

Layout, exactly:
- Top row, left: the HEAD WITHOUT THE CROWN: brown curly hair on top and down both sides, the steel-grey face mask with its two narrow squinting eye slits, the painted brown moustache and the small goatee. The head ends at the chin, no neck.
- Top row, middle: the BODY: the gold cape with its two round gold collar clasps over the shoulders, hanging behind to the calves, and the long royal-blue robe with its gold stripe and hem, and the dark boots, with NO arms, NO sleeves and NO hands at all (the arms are separate parts below): the mantle covers the shoulders and the robe's sides are plain, and no head; a short skin neck stump at the top.
- Top row, right: the BACK ARM (his left arm): a royal-blue sleeve from the shoulder hanging down to a bare skin fist.
- Bottom row, left: the FRONT ARM (his right arm): a royal-blue sleeve from the shoulder, bent at the elbow, ending in a big closed bare skin fist that points to the right.
- Bottom row, middle: the CROWN on its own: the jewelled gold crown with its ball-tipped points and gems, front view, whole, no head under it.
- Right edge, spanning from top to bottom: the SWORD on its own, standing straight up, narrow blade at the top, curled gold crossguard, grip and round gold pommel at the bottom, whole and not held.
